reviews.title: From good to bad
reviews.text: This app used to be very helpful, easy to navigate and intuitive. Now I find that I can’t find anything or use the app as I once did. Seems to me like changes were made that are not beneficial. A quick example would be how I used to keep three or four windows open at a time and now I can’t do that for some reason. I feel like I need a class to operate inside the app. Also the subscription fee is…less than ideal! I have deleted the app from all my devices and will look elsewhere.

reviews.title: Very BUGGY on iPhone and iPad - No fixes so far! Works great on my computers.
reviews.text:
I have been using Logos since the days of Dos operating system.  I like the program a lot, but it was hard to learn to use it effectively.

I use the iPhone and iPad hours each day. But find it now very buggy at times. It locks up, closes the application at times, major issues with highlighting and copy and pasting, at times it will not scroll text, I’ve had it repeat things over and over when scrolling. Some times it even changes the text when you try to copy or highlight to different passages that your not in. 

At other times it works as it supposed to. When it working I give it thumbs up. 5 Stars when having issues a negative 10,000.

Have repeatedly sent reports to support some with pictures of my screen. 

I bought another iPhone and iPad, still having the same issues. When I changed equipment, I downloaded all new apps, I did not restore from backups. Same old issues!!

This has been frustrating to say the least.  

This program on my iPhone was very good, until a few months  ago.  Have friends that have iPhones having trouble as well.

I have bought every upgrade they have come out with. Have spent a few thousand dollars, on this product, just spent another $2500 updating equipment. I’ve upgrades the product the the next to the highest level you can get, that’s expensive, have 2500 resources.

reviews.title: NOW forced to register?
reviews.text:
I have been using Logos, Vyros, & Faithlife study Bible for years. Today I am being forced to register into their "community" & being told I have the wrong status code! No option to opt out or skip! And I am registered with a scholar's library. I use all 3 apps. Will keep trying. Thank you!
Would rate 4 stars otherwise. A few suggestions:
1. Provide a way to track or categorize notes & colors. Eg: If I have a color system can I look at all the verses highlighted blue (God) as a group? This would be very powerful.
2. ESV steady Bible & I think other study resources as well do not align. They keep going back to the overview section. Example: Pr 10:1-22:16 has an intro which is good. But, if I have sync on and am reading pr 15:10 it will take me back to pr 10:1. Love to use sync. Turn it off for overviews.

reviews.title: Getting Worse with Every “Improvement”

What happened to being able to have multiple tabs open? If not for the original language helps and Logos digital resources I’ve purchased, I would simply delete this app and move on.

reviews.title: Disappointed long time user
reviews.text:
Logos is a fully functional, powerful app and works well overall.

As a missionary, I have personally used Logos for many years and have enjoyed its benefits but have been growing increasingly frustrated and disappointed with it. 

The reason I am giving it a single star at this time is because it has become an ecumenical bookstore rather than a quality pastoral resource and tool.  The new books being released are often New Age, geared toward social agendas, emphasizing tradition over truth, or doctrinally weak. When I began to use Logos (7) it had a few of those books available, but Logos/Faithlife (a misnomer) has seemingly chosen the path of appealing to the mass market rather than biblically principled.  Regrettably, I am now stuck in their ecosystem having spent thousands upon thousands of dollars over nearly a decade. 

I am also highly disappointed that Logos/Faithlife has chosen the subscription model as well.  This is a well-designed business model for maximizing profit over quality. The user, in order to maintain the product’s usefulness, must continually pay for “features” regardless of whether they want them or not. Logos claims the user benefits from this “upgrade” but I strongly disagree. The upgrades (so-called) are gimmicks that are rarely used unless one considers a sermon builder essential for hearing from God on a passage. Logos has become bloatware.

reviews.title: If only
reviews.text: I have told many friends and soon-to-be seminary students that Logos Bible Software is like the greatest library in the world that won’t let you in. I am not a tech guy and so all the magical features, that I KNOW logos offers, are completely unavailable to me. Which makes the program more frustrating than I can say. If they ever wanted to do a guy a favor they would hire a full-time on-computer-nerd-guy to shout every moment of the day “Hey! make it easier to access…Hey! make it easier to access…Hey! make it easier to access.” In the time it would take me to learn how to access all the bells and whistles of the program I could master Greek and Hebrew…so I might as well just do that. PLEASE, in God’s Holy Name, make this program easier to use for the non-computer guy…Until then, it sits unopened and unused…as sad reminder that I have great tools at my fingertips that I simply cannot use. It is maddening beyond belief. And yes, I’ve tried the videos that are supposed to teach you…which merely further muddy already muddy waters.

reviews.title: They set up money changing tables in the house of God, and removed the Bible tab!?
reviews.text:
The desktop reader is a marketplace before it’s a library these days, and now they literally removed the Bible tab on mobile, which says to me they aren’t focused anymore on the gospel. Repent of this while there’s still time! I’m moving on unless you guys get serious about the gospel. We don’t wrestle against flesh and blood, but we do wrestle, watch out! Heed my words! Keep your oil lamps lit and full of oil! (Good thing you guys are a dealer, huh? 😆) Ok, I may have to deal with logs in my eye still (Lord Jesus, please guide me), but this money business is a serious speck in the eyes of the brothers in charge at Faithlife Corp. (Lord Jesus, please guide them 🙏). 

I don’t say this lightly. The Gospel is more real than the air we breathe, and the kingdom of God at hand is more tangible than even the paper its herald printed the message on. I didn’t take its extortions serious until consequences rolled in. Please don’t make my mistake!!

reviews.title: AI Heavy, Light on One Step Conventional Tools
reviews.text:
I have loved Logos since 1994 when I started seminary. When the mobile apps came out, I learned to love those too. This review is specific to the last mobile version. 

Logos may be positioning themselves for the future by their AI emphasis. All I can say today is that I pulled out the Bible to search for two words in scripture, and I could not find anything that I recognized as search. I couldn’t even figure out how to limit the AI to a set of books like Paul’s letters for example. I was in a meeting with friends and needed a verse. I had to admit that I couldn’t find one. First time since the mobile apps came out. Maybe there was training announced, but there was nothing in the app itself that warned me that it was going to be different this time than last time. This is the only way I know to get the company’s attention is by giving a negative review. First time ever.

I’m sad.

reviews.title: More and more of a cash grab
reviews.text: I love Logos, and have used it throughout my BA and MA in Biblical Studies program. However ever since they jumped on the subscription model and AI bandwagon, I feel like it’s becoming more and more of a cash grab. I don’t want the AI features and yet every time I do an inline search it automatically performs it and then tells me I have a limited amount of free searches left. However I decided to write today because it now looks like I have to pay for the exact same feature that was free a month ago, which is to highlight a word and see the Hebrew behind it. The idea of paying for a feature that used to be free is ridiculous enough as it is, but even more so when I’ve spent hundreds of dollars on Greek and Hebrew dictionaries. But that doesn’t matter, because I need to upgrade to the new subscription to have the convenience that I’ve always enjoyed. If I hadn’t sunk thousands of dollars into this product I’d be switching to accordance.

reviews.title: What happened?
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for years and logos for even longer. When looking at my Bible word study, the dictionaries I’ve always had now say "not available." At first, I thought all my dictionaries were gone, but after opening a new tab to find my Dictionary, I saw it was there, but for some reason it wasn't showing in the word study section. I want to be able to stay in the same section and see when that word was used, its spelling, and how it was used in both Hebrew and Greek. Now I have to switch between multiple tabs and scroll through multiple dictionaries to find the word, instead of it all being right where it was before. This is very bad, as I want to be able to study using my phone app and provide definitions of keywords during my lectures, Bible Study, Sunday School classes, and sermons. I will check to see if it is doing the same thing on my laptop. Perhaps this is a glitch that was overlooked in an update. Developers, please fix ASAP.

reviews.title: Fraud Alert
reviews.text: So I bought a library soon after logging in. Went to get the 50% off gold library and when I clicked purchase (after entering all my info) it kicked me out. Now I cannot get back in as it states invalid email or password. Mind you, it is auto on my computer and phone. I have logged in and out several times today and now all of a sudden my info is wrong. Ok cool. Password reset. Email sent, click the link and it says page expired. I follow all the instructions of clearing cache, using different browser…all the things, still doesn’t work. Customer service did reply to my first email with the same generic garbage and now they are non existent. Surprise surprise. Requested money back and I’m sure that we t happen. Anyways, not worth the headache, Olive tree is what I already use but was told logos is better. Obviously that was fake news…dang, I fell for it too, just realized this😐. Well if you read this far, don’t fall for it.

reviews.title: Difficult to use
reviews.text: I started out with this software when it was Thompson Chain Bible Study for computer in 1998. It’s been sold and renamed many times over the years. When it was Wordsearch it was the easiest to use and then technology moved to tablets. When I went to iPad instead of computer wordsearch wouldn’t transfer my books to the app and said I would have to buy my books again so I went to Olive Tree app. When I got the notice that another company have bought wordsearch and my books would finally transfer I use it as read only because I had so many notes in Olive Tree. Now logos has the app. I’m sorry but find it very difficult to use this app. I want to like it but I don’t see it happening. It highlights when I don’t want it, simply by trying to move down the page to read. I can’t delete the highlight. The help in totally useless. It wasn’t bad until the last 2 update. I find it very irritating because over the years I have invested thousands of dollars in books that can only be used in the app, I have over 5,000. I admit many I don’t use anymore, the commentaries are the ones I use the most. Please make logos more user friendly or restore wordsearch.
